note: The store whose shelf prices the app shows (crawler/storeprice.py). Walmart's Product Lookup returns a store's own price and stock with storeId; the category listing ignores it, so store prices are fetched 20 items per call after the crawl. Only Walmart's own in-stock offer counts (with storeId Walmart answers with the buy box, a marketplace seller's price when the store does not carry the item: a 15 oz soup at $10, 2026-10-13); anything else is recorded as not carried. Scope and cadence are the tiers: departments outside every tier are never store-priced (the app's live check fetches the store price on demand when online). A row with a store price checked within its tier's max_age_days shows it (labelled with the store); otherwise Walmart.com's price. Measured 2026-10-13 on the first 4,237 priced rows: the store price differs from Walmart.com's for about half of Food, Personal Care, Health and Household rows, so those go first. A row the store does not carry (no Walmart-sold offer: g) is asked again after not_carried_every_days (90), not the tier's cadence: about 60% of consumable rows come back not carried and a store's assortment changes slowly, so the carried rows get their shelf price refreshed sooner (2026-10-14).
